title: Compose Testing and Adaptive Shopping Capstone

scout.purpose: A production UI needs layered evidence for state logic, semantic interaction, accessibility, visual attributes, navigation, and adaptive continuity.
scout.realWorldUse: Compose unit, UI, accessibility, and screenshot tests protect different failure classes in continuous integration and release review.
scout.outcome: Design a test pyramid around semantics and finish an adaptive, accessible shopping slice with deterministic visual and interaction evidence.

sections.title: Test contracts at the cheapest reliable layer

blocks.text: Test pure reducers, formatting, validation, and adaptive decisions as local unit tests. Compose UI tests set content, query semantics, perform actions, and assert observable state; use roles, text, labels, or stable test tags only when user semantics cannot identify the node. The merged tree matches accessibility focus while the unmerged tree helps diagnose descendants. Synchronisation waits for Compose idleness, but external asynchronous work still needs controlled fakes and clocks. Avoid asserting implementation hierarchy or exact recomposition counts.

blocks.caption: The test acts through user-facing semantics and adds automated accessibility checks.

blocks.text: Accessibility checks can flag missing labels, contrast, target size, and traversal problems during instrumented tests, while manual TalkBack and keyboard scripts validate workflow meaning. Navigation graph tests verify destinations separately from content callback tests. Screenshot tests compare rendered output with approved references and are valuable for colour, spacing, typography, and adaptive states, but require controlled fonts, density, locale, animation, device profile, and rendering environment. A golden diff is review evidence, not proof of semantics or interaction.

blocks.title: Tests protect contracts
blocks.text: Query what users perceive and do, not incidental layout nesting or function names.

sections.title: Screenshot and capstone evidence need controlled configurations

blocks.text: The Adaptive Shopping capstone integrates product grid, details, basket, navigation, animation, accessibility, theme, edge-to-edge, and compact/expanded layouts. Scope a vertical slice with local fake data so UI evidence is deterministic before networking arrives. Define acceptance journeys for browse, select variant, add, edit basket, rotate or resize, and recover from invalid stock. Record screenshots for representative configurations and make tests assert user outcomes rather than internal composable structure.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

trap_check.mistake: Updating every changed golden without reviewing the diff.
trap_check.why: A regression becomes the new approved reference.
trap_check.fix: Require a human review tied to the intended design or configuration change.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Build the Level 3 shopping vertical slice with local data, adaptive catalogue and detail, basket flow, animation, themes, accessibility, edge-to-edge, and layered test evidence.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Browse-to-basket works in compact and expanded windows. TalkBack, keyboard, large text, RTL, and dark theme checks are documented. Unit, semantic UI, accessibility, and screenshot tests protect distinct contracts.
